help.intro: A text of about 200 words about the test that a million people have taken: the Einbürgerungstest, the test for German citizenship. Since 2008 everyone who wants a German passport answers 33 questions in 60 minutes, drawn from a pool of 310; 17 right answers are enough, and more than nine out of ten pass. The text tells what is asked, what else you need for the passport, and why many Germans themselves would fail. All facts are real and were checked. You read what you have just learnt: indirect questions with ob and with question words (Wissen Sie, ob …? Man fragt, wie viele Bundesländer Deutschland hat), where the verb goes to the end, and the grammar words you meet in every exercise (die Frage, die Antwort, richtig, falsch, der Satz, das Beispiel). Read for the gist first, then find one number or one rule per question.
help.tips[0].title: Indirect questions: ob and W-words
help.tips[0].text: A question inside a sentence sends its verb to the end. Yes/no question → ob: Hat Deutschland 16 Bundesländer? → Wissen Sie, ob Deutschland 16 Bundesländer hat? W-question → keep the W-word: Wie viele Bundesländer hat Deutschland? → Man fragt, wie viele Bundesländer Deutschland hat. Typical openers: Wissen Sie, …? Können Sie mir sagen, …? Ich möchte wissen, …. Im Test steht, …. Comma before ob and the W-word.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The test asks, for example, when the Wall fell and who elects the Bundestag.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Many want to know whether the test is hard. The answer: over ninety per cent pass it.
help.tips[0].check.q: Direct: Kostet der Test Geld? Indirect: Ich möchte wissen, ____.
help.tips[0].check.why: Yes/no question → ob + clause with the verb at the end.
help.tips[1].title: Grammar words you meet in quizzes
help.tips[1].text: die Frage / die Antwort (question / answer), richtig / falsch (right / wrong), der Satz (sentence), das Wort (word), das Beispiel (example), die Lücke (gap), ankreuzen (to tick), bestehen (to pass: den Test bestehen), durchfallen (to fail), die Prüfung (test, examination), die Punkte (points), die Zeit: 60 Minuten Zeit haben. Also: Mehrfachauswahl = multiple choice, vier Antworten, eine ist richtig.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Every question has four answers, and only one is right. You have to tick it.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: With seventeen right answers you have passed the test.
help.tips[1].check.why: durchfallen = to fail; bestehen = to pass; ankreuzen = to tick.
help.remember[0]: Indirect question: ob for yes/no, W-word for the rest, verb at the end: Wissen Sie, ob … hat?
help.remember[1]: Frage, Antwort, richtig, falsch, ankreuzen, bestehen, durchfallen.
help.exam: Short informative texts about procedures and rules, with indirect questions, are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: 33 questions, 60 minutes, 17 right answers, and most Germans would not pass: read about the citizenship test.
help.vocab[4].example: Man muss Deutsch auf einem mittleren Niveau können.
passageTranslation:
Whoever wants a German passport must take a test: the naturalisation test. It has existed since 2008, and more than a million people have already taken it.

This is how it works: there are 310 questions. In the test you get 33 of them, with four answers per question. Only one answer is right, and you have to tick it. You have 60 minutes. With 17 right answers you have passed. The test costs 25 euros.

What is asked? For example, how many federal states Germany has (16), when the Wall fell (1989), who elects the Bundestag (citizens from 18) or whether you may choose your religion freely in Germany (yes). Three questions are only about the federal state in which you live. Many ask whether the test is hard. The answer: over 90 per cent pass it. All 310 questions are on the internet for practice.

But the test is only one part. You must also know German, at least at an intermediate level, and usually have lived in Germany for five years. You must earn your own money and may not have problems with the police.

A newspaper once asked Germans whether they would pass the test. Many did not know how many federal states there are, or when the constitution was written (1949). The result: many Germans would fail.

questions[0].optionsTranslation[1]: people who want a German passport
questions[0].optionsTranslation[2]: all foreigners who live in Germany for more than a year

questions[1].questionTranslation: How many questions do you get in the test, and how many must be right?
questions[2].options[1]: eine indirekte Frage mit W-Wort, Verb am Ende
questions[2].explanation: The W-word wie viele starts an indirect question; the verb hat moves to the end.
questions[2].questionTranslation: '… how many federal states Germany has.' Which form is that?
questions[2].optionsTranslation[1]: an indirect question with a W-word, verb at the end
questions[2].optionsTranslation[2]: a relative clause with the relative pronoun wie
questions[3].explanation: "… oder ob man in Deutschland seine Religion frei wählen darf (ja)."
questions[3].questionTranslation: May you choose your religion freely in Germany?
questions[4].explanation: ob stands for a yes/no question: Ist der Test schwer?
questions[4].questionTranslation: 'Many ask whether the test is hard.' What is the direct question?
questions[5].questionTranslation: How many people pass the test?
questions[6].options[1]: Deutsch auf mittlerem Niveau, meistens fünf Jahre in Deutschland, eigenes Geld, keine Probleme mit der Polizei
questions[6].explanation: "Man muss auch Deutsch können … meistens fünf Jahre in Deutschland leben. Man muss sein eigenes Geld verdienen und darf keine Probleme mit der Polizei haben."
questions[6].questionTranslation: What else do you need for the passport besides the test?
questions[6].optionsTranslation[1]: German at intermediate level, usually five years in Germany, your own income, no problems with the police
questions[6].optionsTranslation[2]: a German spouse and two witnesses who speak for you
questions[7].explanation: "Viele wussten nicht, wie viele Bundesländer es gibt … Das Ergebnis: Viele Deutsche würden durchfallen."
questions[7].questionTranslation: What did the newspaper find out?
questions[7].optionsTranslation[0]: All Germans pass the test easily because they learnt the answers at school.
questions[7].optionsTranslation[1]: Many Germans would fail because, for example, they do not know the number of federal states.
